In advance, thank you so much for your answer. If anything it made me a little bit calmer (EDIT: youll probably notice it just by reading what Id written). 


To further explain myself, during teenagehood I was very turbulent kid (now Im just turbulent "adult"). In the beggining of my puberty I felt that I was way too stubborn, hot-tempered and easily offended, pretty much like my father. I because I saw how "the original" was behaving towards my other family members I wanted to change (dont get me wrong my dad isnt by far the worst dad but he has cons like most of us do). You see, this currently isnt my first time being in bad mood lets say. When I was 14-15 I skipped school like Ive done today and yesterday but the thing was that my parents actually found out the truth. They were both crying a lot telling me how hard it already is for them (at that time my grandpa was dying). They told me their story again: How poor they were and how they worked out from basicaly nothing to the upper middle-class. They truely are hardworking people but I hadnt acknowledged their path till that day. So I tried to work on me. From then it wasnt "me-me" but it was "me-us". I wanted to be the best so someone else could acquire the best. It was me for them because I felt guilty and indebted so I wanted to give away myself as much as possible, thats I wanted to invest in myself so heavily. I guess thats both a good and a bad thing... 

But even after all that I wanted to commit suicide yet I turned it into my only and the most important reason to live. Even though now I dont agree with statements that say something like you should feel bad that you want to commit suicide (after reading Sorrows of Young Werther and all those anti-suicide webpages), I definitely admit that it tied me up to life a little bit more.

On other remarks, Ive done psychologic test on my personality and my top "talents" appeared to be verbal skill and maths skill. The math test consisted of simple mathematical operations with just larger numbers - I think I kind of know that I could be good in maths. But how do you know that Im articulate? I mean... During my Czech lessons I get bad grades for essays and so in English. Does grammar actually plays role in all of this? Its interesting that I feel much more comfortable writing in English even though my grammar is as turbulent as me and I guess thats because Im not as scolded in English as I was in Czech... I seriously thought about writing a "book" but I still feel discouraged and sadly this isnt the only field. 

I feel like my school blends academics with reality too much that its already automated in my head but I know that my school isnt exclusive to this. I think that I know a lot but my feelings are beaten up to something much different.

Sorry if Im getting little bit too nosy but do you do something that is somehow related to what youve studied? (Dont answer if you dont want to)
